title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Healthcare Assistant (HCA)

Locations: Kent, London, Reading, Suffolk and Isle of Wight
Employer: GK Healthcare
Job Type: Flexible shifts Full-time and Part-time opportunities

Job Overview

GK Healthcare is recruiting dedicated and compassionate Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to work across care homes in Kent, London, Reading, Suffolk and the Isle of Wight.

We offer flexible shift opportunities for experienced Healthcare Assistants who are passionate about providing high-quality care and supporting residents with their daily needs.

Whether you are looking for regular shifts or greater flexibility around your existing commitments, GK Healthcare can help you find opportunities that suit your availability.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide personal care and support to residents with dignity and respect.
- Assist residents with daily living activities, including washing, dressing and mobility.
- Support residents with their physical and emotional well-being.
- Monitor residents' conditions and report any concerns to the relevant senior staff.
- Maintain accurate care records and follow individual care plans.
- Follow safeguarding, infection prevention and health and safety procedures.
- Work effectively with care home teams to deliver high-quality care.

Essential Requirements
- Previous experience as a Healthcare Assistant in a UK care home or nursing home.
- A compassionate, caring and professional attitude.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills.
- Knowledge of personal care, safeguarding and infection prevention.
- Valid DBS on the Update Service.
- Up-to-date mandatory training certificates, including practical Moving and Handling training where required.
- The right to work in the UK.

Why Join GK Healthcare?
- Flexible shifts to suit your availability.
- Opportunities across multiple locations.
- Support from our dedicated recruitment team.
- Assistance with registration and compliance.
- Opportunities to build experience across different care settings.
- Ongoing communication and support throughout your assignment.

Apply Today

Are you a reliable and compassionate Healthcare Assistant looking for your next opportunity?

Join GK Healthcare and take the next step in your healthcare career.

Please send your CV and contact details, and our recruitment team will get in touch.

title: Residential Childcare Worker
description:
Support Worker - Children's Home
Location: Berkshire - Reading
Hourly rate: National Living Wage, with rates of up to £13.15 per hour (depending on experience)
Job Type: Temporary, Agency Work
Shift Pattern: Flexible shifts available, including days, nights, sleep-ins, weekends and long days.

About the Role:

At First for Support, we're looking for compassionate and reliable Children's and Young People's Support Workers to join our growing team, providing temporary staffing to children's homes in and around Reading.

As a Support Worker, you'll play an important role in supporting children and young people in residential care settings. You will help provide a safe, supportive and nurturing environment, build positive relationships and support young people with their daily routines, activities, education and emotional wellbeing. No two days are the same, giving you the opportunity to make a real difference while enjoying the flexibility that temporary work offers.

Your Responsibilities:

As a Children's Support Worker, your responsibilities may include:
Provide high-quality care and support to children and young people.
Build positive and trusting relationships.
Support daily routines, activities and independence.
Promote positive behaviour and emotional wellbeing.
Follow care plans, risk assessments and safeguarding procedures.
Complete accurate daily records and reports.
Work effectively as part of a team and alongside other professionals.

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for candidates who:
Have previous experience in a similar role as a Children's Support Worker.
Are reliable, professional and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
Have excellent communication and interpersonal skills and enjoy building meaningful relationships.
Are Caring, patient and resilient.
Are able to remain calm in challenging situations.
Committed to safeguarding and promoting children's welfare.

In return, we offer weekly pay, flexible temporary shifts, ongoing support from a dedicated recruitment consultant and the opportunity to work with a variety of trusted care providers across Hampshire, gaining valuable experience across different care settings.

If you're passionate about supporting children and young people and making a positive difference in their lives, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and a member of the First for Support team will be in touch to discuss your application.

Please note: First for Support is unable to offer sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK, as we do not provide Skilled Worker visa sponsorship.

title: Youth Support Worker - Reading
description:
Youth Support Worker - Reading

We have an exciting opportunity for a compassionate and dedicated Youth Support Worker to join a specialist school in Reading supporting students aged 5 to 11 with Social, Emotional, and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, many of whom also experience behavioural challenges.

This role is vital in a nurturing and structured environment where every child benefits from a personalised Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). You will work closely with students to support their emotional regulation, behavioural development, and academic progress, helping them build resilience and confidence to thrive both inside and beyond school.

Our school uses restorative practices to empower students in managing their emotions and behaviours, setting them on a path towards positive personal growth and success. You'll be an integral part of a team committed to creating a safe, supportive space that fosters wellbeing and learning.

What you'll bring to the role:
- A patient, kind, and empathetic approach to working with children facing SEMH and behavioural difficulties
- A positive mindset and a passion for helping young people overcome their challenges
- Willingness to learn and adapt to the individual needs of each child
- Previous experience working with children, particularly those with SEMH or behavioural needs, is desirable but not essential

Why this role is important:
You'll be supporting students who need extra emotional and behavioural support to engage successfully in their learning. Your contribution will help them achieve personalised goals and develop essential life skills that prepare them for the next stages of their education and life beyond school.

Whether you're a graduate seeking experience or someone passionate about making a difference in the community, this role offers valuable hands-on experience and professional development in a specialist SEMH setting.

Details:
- Location: Reading
- Term-time role
- Salary: 90 - 100 per day
- Start date: ASAP
- Small class sizes with strong senior leadership support

If you're ready to make a real difference and grow your skills in a specialist SEMH environment, apply now! Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis, so don't delay.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Night Support Worker SL6
description:
Night Support Worker, Maidenhead, SL6. £18.93 gross per hour for weekday waking hours and £12.71 gross per hour for sleeping hours. A rewarding opportunity to support a happy, engaging 14-year-old boy who has cerebral palsy, epilepsy, significant learning difficulties and is autistic. Help Ethan enjoy a reassuring night-time routine and start each school day feeling comfortable and prepared.

Key Information
- Job Title: Night Support Worker
- Pay: £18.93 gross per hour waking hours; £12.71 gross per hour sleeping hours; £21.01 gross per hour weekend waking hours; £37.86 gross per hour public holidays. Approximately £18,112.00 gross per annum.
- Location: Maidenhead, SL6
- Hours and Days of Work: Tuesday and Thursday, 9:00 PM 8:30 AM the following morning, compromising of waking support and sleeping shift.
- Essential Experience: Experience supporting children or young people with special educational needs or disabilities.
- Driver Required: No
- Recruiter: Jade Bariesheff

Ethan, 14, is a happy, engaging boy who enjoys music, sensory toys, cause-and-effect activities and family time. He has cerebral palsy, epilepsy, significant learning difficulties and is autistic, and benefits from familiar routines, clear communication and one-to-one support.

This is a rewarding opportunity for a patient, reliable Support Worker who can provide calm overnight reassurance and help Ethan prepare for school. Experience supporting children or young people with additional needs is essential, alongside a commitment to safeguarding, dignity and person-centred care. The role combines waking support and a sleeping shift.

Interested? Visit the Snap Care Website for full job details.
